rationale: Accepted: kd should be near zero, since the critique's arithmetic is right that a 1.5 signal step with kd=0.05 gives a turn kick of about 2600 PWM and sensor noise would trigger it repeatedly. I set kd to 0.01, a small damper, rather than zero, so a little derivative action remains. Partly accepted: kp=6 is large and unverified, and at 350 PWM per turn unit it gives up to about 3150 PWM of steering at full signal, so I reduced kp to 3.5. That still gives about 1.75 turn units (about 610 PWM) at a half-tape offset, which is firm enough to recover from bends. Accepted in part on the motor mismatch: the fixed left/right bias is a steady offset the integrator must absorb, so I raised ki from 0.1 to 0.2. With the integral clamp at +/-2, that is at most 0.4 turn units (about 140 PWM), which is a modest correction, not a windup risk. Partly rejected on speed: I kept the speed plan but raised base_speed from 1.8 to 1.9 for a little more margin against the 3 s limit, since a failed finish loses the 500-point completion term. Speed is still unverified against real ground speed because the inputs do not map PWM to m/s, so this is a judgement, not a measured result. Sensors, geometry, sensor weights and last_direction line-loss handling are unchanged: the critique confirmed the layout covers the 25 mm tape and the antisymmetric weights are sound. I kept the full measurement list so the next round can tell whether the slalom oscillates (steering_oscillation, max_error) or the robot runs short of time (completion_time, progress). Expected result: completion on oval and s-bend with lower jitter than the draft; the slalom is still the main risk, and these numbers are guesses until telemetry exists.
